name: Premier Energies Ltd
title: Premier Energies Ltd - 544238 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Premier Energies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR2,656 crore, with PAT up 30.8% to INR462 crore and a INR16,260 crore order book.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR2,656 crore, EBITDA rose 17.8% to INR760 crore and PAT rose 30.8% to INR462 crore. Solar manufacturing EBITDA margin was 29.3% and PAT margin 17.9%, with PAT margin moderating on higher depreciation and lower other income. Management flagged a 7 GW TOPCon cell line at Naidupeta as commissioned with commercial production expected later in November, and a fresh INR4,001 crore cell and module order intake. Working capital rose on raw material inventory, which management called temporary.

financial_highlights.change: moderated slightly on higher depreciation and lower other income
new cell and module order wins of INR4,001 crore in quarter

segments.name: Solar cells and modules
segments.commentary: Order book split is about 48% cells and 48% modules, with about 20% of the module book being DCR; 68-70% of the total book is domestic DCR manufacturing. Non-DCR is 25-30% of the book at single-digit EBITDA margins and realisations above INR12.75/W.

segments.name: Transformers (new capacity)
segments.commentary: 4 GVA of new capacity is being commissioned and type testing is complete for all power transformer ranges except EHV. Management says normalised margin is about 15%, after 12% in Q2 versus about 22% in the prior quarter.

segments.name: Transcon (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR122 crore, PAT INR18 crore, EBITDA margin 15% and PAT margin 8% in the quarter.

segments.name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: Operationalisation expected in Q2 2027 through cell-to-pack and pack-to-container lines, in partnership with German firm RCT. LFP cell supply is not yet tied up; sourcing is from Chinese tier-1 makers.

guidance_outlook: Naidupeta 7 GW cell line: CUF ramp to 25-30% in December and about 70% by end-March 2027.
Capex for the next two quarters moderates to about INR700 crore, implying about INR2,400 crore for FY27.
Management expects a significant step-up in financial performance as Naidupeta and Seetharampur volumes ramp up over the next few quarters.
Annual industry capacity addition expected to reach about 50 GW AC this year, above last year.
Ingot-wafer Phase 1 targeted for December 2027 and Phase 2 (additional 5 GW, total about 10 GW) for June 2028, subject to government timing.
Transformer revenue expected to more than treble over three years, with capacity ramping to 80-90% over three years.
Order book of about 10 GW to execute over 12-14 months.
US cell factory with JV partner: site finalisation targeted in 12-18 months.
Depreciation for FY27 about INR600 crore, per management.
capex_capacity: 7 GW TOPCon cell line at Naidupeta commissioned; trial runs under way; commercial production expected later in November 2026. ALMM enrolment inspection by NISE expected in the third week of November.
Ingot-wafer project on 169 acres at Naidupeta, with land, water, and power approvals in place; wafer vendor deposit made and agreements under Chinese export-control registration.
Inventory build-up is largely raw material, linked to Seetharampur and Naidupeta ramp-up plus shipping congestion; management expects normalisation by March 2027 quarter.
Chinese draft export control on high-end equipment: cell line machinery already imported; ingot-wafer equipment sourcing dependent on clarity after 15 November.
demand_pricing: DCR module realisations: retail about INR23-24/W; KUSUM C and C&I about INR21.5; IPP about INR20 for next year; blended DCR average about INR21.5-22/W.
Non-DCR module pricing has fallen from INR14-15/W a year ago to about INR12.5/W; Premier realises INR12.75-13/W; competitors accept sub-INR12.
Cell prices: Mono PERC USD0.12-0.125/W, TOPCon USD0.14-0.145/W.
Management says a SECI bid at about INR17-18/W was an introductory price, not a market benchmark; an INR18 DCR quote reported in the market is also not seen as a benchmark.
Mix: retail about 35-40% of the order book; no QoQ mix disclosure.
Demand: management views demand at about 50-60 GW against supply, which should match or exceed supply for 12-18 months; pure-play module makers face difficulty.
Input costs: recent increases in aluminium, copper and polymer film hit module assembly profitability; silver has eased; wafer prices from China fluctuating.

Cell order book fell QoQ because no new merchant cell orders were booked; cells are increasingly used captively as module capacity (5.6 GW) was commissioned. Management says there were no order cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the cell order book fall more than cell revenue recognised in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no new merchant cell orders were booked in the quarter; cells are increasingly used captively as the new 5.6 GW module line came on stream. No order cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 2,400 crore FY27 capex still on track and what is the spend profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Most cell and module expansion capex is complete; remaining spend covers Naidupeta, battery, aluminium and open-access captive projects. Capex about INR700 crore per quarter for the next two quarters, totalling about INR2,400 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the battery (BESS) plan enough to meet the 40% localisation rule without more capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cell-to-pack and pack-to-container lines plus Indian EMS and localised components should meet 40% easily, with no additional capex needed. LFP cells are still to be contracted from China.

qa_highlights.question: Are the margins and pricing on the order book at current levels, and what is the risk from low-priced DCR orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders were booked at current prices, and management hopes to hold margins subject to cost volatility. It views the SECI at about INR17-18 and the INR18 quote as introductory and not benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the transformer margin normal level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the normalised transformer margin is about 15%; the prior quarter's 22% was boosted by steel and copper price increases and hedged inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any block sale or QIP risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied a GEF block or promoter sale and said the QIP was only an enabling resolution; no QIP is planned, with internal cash flow funding the capex.

risks_watch: China's draft export controls on advanced equipment: final outcome expected in 3-4 weeks; ingot-wafer equipment timelines (Phase 1 December 2027) depend on it.
Non-DCR pricing pressure and rising aluminium, copper and film costs; margin guidance is subject to cost volatility.
Working capital: raw material inventory build-up; management targets normalisation by the March 2027 quarter.
Naidupeta ALMM enrolment inspection (expected third week of November) and the 70% CUF target by March 2027.
BESS cell sourcing is unconfirmed: no firm LFP supply tie-up with Chinese suppliers.
US factory: JV partner in place, site decision in 12-18 months; no capex size given.
Transformer ramp-up: type testing and customer acceptance for large units take 8-12 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, the Naidupeta ramp and policy tailwinds, but cautious and evasive on China export controls, BESS cell sourcing and non-DCR margins. Several answers deferred to the final policy outcome, and management declined to give quarterly DCR mix or product-level spreads.
key_quotes: We expect project commissioning progress to accelerate over the next six months, taking the annual capacity addition to around 50 GW AC territory, surpassing last year's numbers.
There is no block from the promoters. There is no block planned even in the next couple of quarters or even the couple of years.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: US cell factory with JV partner
rows.why: JV partner is in place and site finalisation is targeted in 12-18 months; no capex size was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the Naidupeta ramp and policy tailwinds, but cautious on China export controls, BESS LFP cell sourcing and non-DCR margins; analysts probed cell order book decline, margin sustainability on low-priced DCR orders, and transformer margin normalisation.
